newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indofood owners to reduce stake - report.
newsitem.headline: Indofood owners to reduce stake - report.

text.p: The Salim Group, which owns a controlling stake in Indonesia's largest noodle maker PT Indofood Sukses Makmur, will reduce its holding in the company to about 60 percent from 70 percent, Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported on Friday.

The newspaper quoted Salim Group executive Benny Santoso as saying that the group approved of a bid by tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna, who heads cigarette firm PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, to take a 15 percent stake in Indofood.
"That's why we will increase the free float to about 40 percent," Santoso was quoted as saying.
Salim Group officials could not be immediately reached for comment.
On Thursday, Ekadharmajanto Kasih, chief financial officer of Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, told Reuters that Putera Sampoerna has long-term plans to take a 15 percent stake in Indofood.
Kasih confirmed that Sampoerna had bought a 5.63 percent stake in Indofood on Tuesday.
Indofood was down 125 rupiah at 5,650 in early trade on Friday in an overall weak market. The Jakarta composite index was down 5.47 points, or about 0.82 percent, at 664.52 points at the time.
Santoso told Bisnis Indonesia that currently the Salim Group held about 70 percent of Indofood, with group company PT Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa owning 50.94 percent.

Commenting on Putera Sampoerna's plan to procure about a 15 percent stake in Indofood, Santoso said: "We really understand his point that for his investment, Sampoerna wants some substantial portion."
Santoso also spoke of the possibility of creating an alliance between Indofood and Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, possibly in the distribution area.
"We haven't discussed it yet, but it's one of the possibilities," he said.
